seoTitle: How to Connect Google Chat With Trello
metaDescription: Add the Google Chat Power-Up to a Trello board so card updates, due dates, and comments stream directly into your team's chat space.
intro: Switching between Google Chat and Trello to catch every board update wastes time your team could spend on actual work. The connection lives on Trello's side as a Power-Up rather than something you set up by hunting through Google Chat's own app directory — you add it to a specific board, point it at a Google Chat space, and pick exactly which card events are worth a notification. This guide walks through logging in, finding the Power-Up, and configuring alerts so your chat space gets useful signal instead of noise.

steps.heading: Log into Trello
steps.body: Head to Trello's login screen and sign in with your email, or use one of the faster options underneath — Google, Microsoft, Apple, or Slack, plus a Passkey option if you've set one up. If your organization uses Atlassian for other tools like Jira or Confluence, this is the same account, so check whether you already have credentials before creating a new one.

image.caption: Trello's login screen, with email sign-in plus quick options for Google, Microsoft, Apple, Slack, or a saved passkey.

steps.heading: Open the board you want to connect
steps.body: From your Trello home, the Boards view lists Recently Viewed boards up top and everything under Your Workspaces below, organized by workspace. Pick the specific board whose activity you want streaming into chat — the Power-Up you're about to add applies at the board level, so a team juggling multiple boards will need to repeat this setup on each one that needs alerts.

image.caption: The Trello Boards dashboard, showing Recently Viewed boards and the full board grid under Your Workspaces.

steps.heading: Open Power-Ups on the board
steps.body: Inside the board, open the Power-Ups menu from the top toolbar to bring up the Power-Ups directory. It opens on Featured, a grid of popular add-ons like cross-board field sharing, bulk card actions, and time tracking, with a left-hand sidebar to filter by category — Automation, Communication & Collaboration, IT & Project Management, and more. Use the search box at the top if you already know the name of what you're looking for rather than scrolling categories.

image.caption: Trello's Power-Ups directory open to Featured, with a category sidebar and search field for finding a specific integration.

steps.heading: Find and review the Google Chat Power-Up
steps.body: Search "Google Chat" and open its listing, published by Atlassian with an install base over 50,000. The description explains exactly what it does: it streams updates to Google Chat whenever activity happens on your Trello cards, lists, and boards, and you customize which types of alerts you actually want. The listing spells out concrete examples — someone adding themselves to a card or being assigned one, an attachment added that needs feedback, a card moving from one list to another, or a due date being marked done or shifted — which is worth reading before you add it so you already know what's configurable on the next screen.

image.caption: The Google Chat Power-Up's detail page, listing example alert types like card assignments, attachments, list moves, and due date changes.

steps.heading: Add the Power-Up and connect your space
steps.body: Click Add to install it on the board, which prompts you to authorize the connection to your Google account and select the specific Google Chat space that should receive updates. This is also the point where Trello confirms its data handling is covered under its own privacy practices, worth a skim if you're rolling this out for a team rather than just yourself.

steps.heading: Choose which alerts actually fire
steps.body: Once connected, open the Power-Up's settings from the board to check the specific boxes for the events you want — card assignments, new comments, list moves, due date changes, and so on. Resist the urge to check everything: a chat space that pings for every single card edit gets muted within a week, so start narrow with the events your team actually acts on and expand later if something important is getting missed.

steps.heading: Save and confirm the test alert
steps.body: Save your settings, then make a small real change on the board — move a card, add a comment, assign yourself to something — and check that the corresponding alert shows up in your Google Chat space within a few seconds. If nothing arrives, double back to the Power-Up's settings and confirm the correct space is still selected and at least one event type is checked.

faq.question: Do I need admin access in both Trello and Google Chat?
faq.answer: You need permission to add Power-Ups on the Trello board and the ability to authorize app connections in the target Google Chat space, so check both before starting.

faq.question: Where do I actually set this up — in Trello or Google Chat?
faq.answer: In Trello. The Google Chat Power-Up is installed and configured from the board's Power-Ups menu, not from Google Chat's own app directory.

faq.question: Can I choose which card events trigger a notification?
faq.answer: Yes — the Power-Up's settings let you check specific boxes for events like assignments, comments, list moves, or due date changes, so you're not stuck with every possible alert.

faq.question: What if my chat space gets too noisy with alerts?
faq.answer: Go back into the Power-Up's configuration and uncheck the less useful triggers — most teams do better starting narrow and adding more event types only if something important gets missed.

faq.question: How do I confirm the integration is working?
faq.answer: Make a small change on the board — move a card or add a comment — and check that a matching alert appears in the connected Google Chat space within a few seconds.
